rationale: dc is a compute-heavy NPB serial benchmark dominated by large data-aggregation routines (MultiWayMerge, SharedSortAggregate, ComputeGivenGroupbys, PrefixedAggregate) with tight inner loops over small total text (~29.7 KB, 75 functions), so runtime cost must be strongly penalized for loop-resident transforms: FLA and BCF get low RuntimeCost weights (0.15/0.2) so only functions where the selector sees low execution frequency receive them, while SUB and SPLIT, which are essentially free and semantics-preserving, get high weights across security/diversity/runtime/size dimensions to act as the low-risk baseline layer. IBR is favored moderately (RuntimeCost 0.45) since indirect-branch insertion disrupts static CFG recovery with acceptable cost outside the hottest merge loops. ICALL and IGV hinder static call-graph and global-variable analysis but carry the highest correctness risk through function-signature and linkage perturbation, so they get high SecurityGain/DiversityGain (0.6) but low RuntimeCost (0.25-0.3) and elevated CorrectnessRisk weights (0.3-0.35) so the selector restricts them to well-typed, non-interface functions; correctness preservation is prioritized overall by keeping CorrectnessRisk weights low for all cheap, provably-safe passes.
